- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:894-899 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The merged-fix-up arm incorrectly relies on the exit code of `unblock_try_regrant` to determine if a re-grant attempt was successful.
  WHY: `unblock_try_regrant` always returns 0, regardless of success or failure. The arm enters the `if unblock_try_regrant` body in both cases. When the attempt fails (e.g. actuation failure), the code proceeds to check `UNBLOCK_REGRANT_RESULT`, finds it is `failed`, and executes `return 0`, which terminates the arm entirely. This skips the pending operator-handoff check and the protected handoff check, leaving the issue blocked without creating a handoff comment or notifying an operator.

  WHY: Any call to `followup_handoff_ops` will raise a `NameError` at runtime, causing the handoff action to crash.

- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:891-904, 966-970; the pending-handoff check is at 1006-1026. | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: A pending operator handoff does not reliably hold the issue. The merged-fix-up path calls `unblock_try_regrant` before checking `.handoff_pending`; after the fix-up wait is marked done, later runs also reach the deterministic re-grant at lines 968-970 before the hold check.
  WHY: If the current grant accepts the rejected paths while the issue remains `scope-blocked`, `unblock_try_regrant` runs `regrant_ops`, which invokes `reset_ops` and posts a resume command (`scripts/unblock_actions.py:831, 437-441`). The issue resumes without the person clearing the block, contrary to the handoff’s hold behavior.

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:891-908 (the `if unblock_try_regrant; then` block before the `if jq -e '.handoff_pending == true'` check) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The merged-fix-up arm tries `unblock_try_regrant` before checking whether a protected-path handoff is already pending. When the current guard now grants the rejected paths, `unblock_try_regrant` succeeds, posts the resume command, and returns — bypassing the pending-handoff check at line 905.
  WHY: After a handoff is recorded (the hold marker `<!-- ai:unblock-wait:v1 item=<n> reason=operator_handoff run=<r> -->` is posted and the operator is paged), a later judge run can see that the grant now passes. The regrant path resumes the issue and marks the fix-up wait done, but the handoff marker is not cleared. The operator sees a stale handoff marker and acts on an already-resolved issue. The test `test_judge_merged_fixup_with_a_pending_hold_marks_the_wait_done` disables regrant (`UNBLOCK_JUDGE_REGRANT_ENABLED="false"`), so it does not cover the case where both a pending handoff and a passing grant coexist. The existing deterministic regrant exit outside the fix-up wait (line ~951) also resumes before the handoff check, compounding the bypass.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
